text.title: Design QA During Build Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on whether a stated spec and a reachable running build both exist, how the pass is being run, and what happens to logged deviations at branch cut — to a full QA cycle, a scan-first or states-matrix correction, a sign-off gate, or a skip to CI lint.

decision-tree.root-question: Is there a separate design spec to diff against, and can a running build be reached before release?

branch.when: the surface is designed in code with no separate source of truth — no stated expected value exists to diff against

conclusion.verdict: skip: with no spec every finding is an opinion and the sign-off gate becomes a negotiation the designer loses under release pressure — run token-usage lint in CI instead

branch.when: no build is reachable before release; only exported screenshots or a PR preview image exist

conclusion.verdict: skip and fix the pipeline first: without a reachable `build_ref` no deviation can be reproduced or verified as fixed, so the cadence cannot execute

branch.when: a spec exists and a running build is reachable by commit SHA plus deploy URL, or by build number
branch.question: How is the pass about to be run over that build?

branch.when: the plan is to open mock and build side by side and compare by eye

conclusion.verdict: run the static scan over the diff first — literal colours, spacing, radii, font sizes, z-index — and log every literal with a token equivalent; eyeballing cannot catch a one-digit hex difference that will not move when the token moves

branch.when: a build exists but the review is being done against exported screenshots or a preview image out of habit

conclusion.verdict: run against the running build and record `build_ref` on every deviation; screenshots freeze one viewport with one state and one successfully loaded font, and drift lives in the states they cannot contain

branch.when: only the default state of each screen is on the audit list

conclusion.verdict: declare the states matrix per screen — empty, loading, error, maximum-length content, 320 CSS px width, 200% zoom or the largest dynamic-type step, RTL where shipped; a screen checked only in its default state counts as zero screens audited

branch.when: static scan first, states matrix declared per screen, and `build_ref` recorded on every entry

conclusion.verdict: apply the full methodology: scan, states matrix, on-device target and focus checks, cause-classified deviations, and a sign-off gate before branch cut

branch.when: deviations are already logged and the release branch is about to be cut
branch.question: What state is the deviation log in as the branch cut approaches?

branch.when: target geometry and focus order were read off the mock rather than measured on the rendered build

conclusion.verdict: measure on the build against the platform minimum — 24x24 CSS px for WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8, 44x44 pt Apple HIG, 48x48 dp Material — and tab the running build for focus order and a visible indicator; hit area is not the drawn area

branch.when: entries carry no cause class, so a missing token, a silent spec and a local bug all get the same patch

conclusion.verdict: classify each entry implementation-drift, spec-gap or system-gap, and route every system-gap to the design-system impact queue with its item id — otherwise the identical deviation reappears next sprint on another screen

branch.when: severity-1 entries — accessibility failures or brand and legal-visible errors — are open and the plan is to carry them into next sprint

conclusion.verdict: hold the branch cut: every deviation resolves to a fix ticket id or a named designer's accept-as-is, `remaining_open` carries no severity-1 entry, and `drift_count` equals the length of `deviation_log`
